what: Cross-section parameters the fabricator publishes for its impedance calculation, plus the plating it applies; everything a check needs besides the stackup. Another fabricator = another file of the same keys, read by the board scripts and asserted against the constants they use.
source: JLCPCB impedance calculator assumptions and capabilities pages, published in mil and converted at reading (1 mil = 25.4 µm); re-read on the fabricator's site at each review and date the reading
notes: outer_copper_finished is the base copper plus plating, the thickness the impedance solver uses for an outer track; the trapezoid top width is the base width minus etch_top_width_reduction
solder_mask_on_laminate is c1 of the 2D solver, solder_mask_on_copper is c2: convert against the definition of each parameter, not its position in a list

via_plating is the barrel thickness of the DC-drop mesh, the average hole plating JLCPCB publishes (18 µm, capabilities page, read 2026-11); the hole size of the design (KiCad's via or pad hole, written as is in the drill file) is the FINISHED hole, after plating (JLCPCB capabilities: the tolerance on plated holes, +0.13/-0.08 mm, applies to the finished hole size around the hole size of the file), so the barrel's mean diameter is hole + plating
etch_tolerance_per_flank is the width excursion explored on a few cross-sections (±10 µm per flank), not a guaranteed figure
